requirement:
R1 — GENE/TRANSCRIPT VIEW. A user searches a gene symbol, RefSeq, ENSG or ENST and lands on one transcript page that renders (a) the 5'UTR and 3'UTR nucleotide sequences with every called motif highlighted in place, (b) the protein sequence with every called protein motif highlighted in place, (c) the per-nucleotide NTScore beneath the two UTRs, (d) the annotation evidence attached to each motif (CLIP/miRNA on the RNA side; InterPro/UniProt/MobiDB/SignalP on the protein side), and (e) — the point of the paper — the coupling between the two languages *in this transcript*: which protein-motif cluster present here forms a phylogenetically-gated pair with which UTR-motif cluster present here. Every highlight must be clickable into its cluster (R2) and its module (R3), every absence must be an explained state rather than a blank, and the whole view must be a citable URL.

MEASUREMENTS I MADE THAT CHANGE THE DESIGN (all run with /opt/anaconda3/envs/bio/bin/python, scripts in .../scratchpad/r1cat/):
1. PROTEIN MOTIFS CAN LIVE ON THE SAME NUCLEOTIDE AXIS AS UTR MOTIFS. cds_sequence length == 3*len(protein_sequence) + 3 for 19,210/19,210 rows (stop codon included; 99.84% start ATG, 100% end in a stop). So the exact projection is mRNA_start = len(utr5) + 3*motif_start, mRNA_end = len(utr5) + 3*motif_end + 2. Verified against real codons on ACTB (aa 23-27 DDAPR -> mRNA 153-167 -> GACGATGCCCCCCGG). No candidate design used this; all four drew three disconnected axes. This single fact enables the unified-axis layout and the in-transcript coupling arcs.
2. IN-TRANSCRIPT COUPLING IS VIABLE BUT MUST BE RANKED. Counting co-present gated cluster pairs per transcript (2,620 edges from phylo_corrected_candidates.csv against each transcript's own cluster set): mean 8.04, median 2, p75 7, p90 23, p99 88, max 203; 11,792/18,093 transcripts (65.2%) have >=1; 17.2% exceed 12 and would become a hairball. ACTB has exactly 3. SOX2 33, MLXIPL 12, RET 12. So arcs default to top-N by phylo_corrected_score, never "draw them all".
3. "COLOR BY CLUSTER" IS NOT A LEGITIMATE ENCODING. Distinct motif_clusters per transcript: median 26, p90 55, p99 80, max 108. 13.7% of transcripts have <=12. A 26-way categorical palette is not perceptually resolvable, so cluster identity must live in labels/selection/tooltip, and fill must encode module (6 + unassigned) or region.
4. THE NTSCORE DOMAIN IS ROUGHLY [-8, 0], NOT [-5, 0]. Over 1,200 sampled transcripts per file: utr3 min -7.688, utr5 min -7.281, max never above -0.002 (the score is strictly negative). A [-5,0] domain clips real data.
5. NTSCORE ALIGNMENT IS EXACT FOR THE PORTAL'S UNIVERSE. For all 18,093 motif-bearing transcripts, both HDF5 arrays are present and array length == region sequence length: 18,093/18,093 aligned, 0 misaligned, 0 missing, in BOTH files. But the 3'UTR file holds 18,585 keys, and among the 492 extras I found length mismatches — the build must restrict to the 18,093 and assert.
6. THE "7,784 nt MODEL CONTEXT CAP" IS AN ARTIFACT OF THE WRONG COLUMN. transcript_length is not the mRNA length (ACTB: 1,059 vs actual 84+1,128+600 = 1,812; it is shorter than utr5+cds+utr3 in 19,210/19,210 rows). Real mRNA length = len(utr5)+len(cds)+len(utr3): motif-bearing median 2,923, p99 8,736, max 11,426; motif-free median 10,749, max 109,224 (TTN). 445 transcripts exceed 11,426 and all lack motifs, but 672 under it also lack motifs. The empty state must NOT quote 7,784 nt as a hard cap.
7. LONG PROTEIN MOTIFS ARE LESS ALARMING THAN FEARED. Protein motif_length median 8, p99 54, max 535, but as a fraction of its own protein: median 0.013, p99 0.118, max 0.464. Zero instances cover >50% of a protein; 126 cover >25%.
8. THE MOTIF LAYER IS SINGLE-LANE BY PROOF; ONLY ANNOTATION LAYERS NEED PACKING. Max stacking depth is exactly 1 across all 53,367 (transcript, region) groups (survey, exhaustive), and projected protein motifs occupy CDS coordinates disjoint from UTR motifs — so one lane is valid across the entire mRNA. InterPro (median 5, max 436 domains/transcript), UniProt features and 4-method CLIP peaks DO overlap and need interval packing.
9. ACTB (NM_001101) IS THE RIGHT DEFAULT. 3 utr5 motifs (all utr5_0004), 13 utr3, 4 protein (all prot_0040) — and prot_0040 x utr5_0004 is the single highest-scoring gated pair in the whole analysis (phylo_corrected_score 1.7694, co_count 175, 23 clades, frac_co_ZNF 0.000). It exercises coordinates, join, projection, clustering, annotation and coupling in one screen.
10. A CLUSTER LABEL CAN CONTRADICT ITS OWN INSTANCE'S ANNOTATION. ACTB's protein motifs are in prot_0040, whose top cluster-level enrichment is "Histone-fold" (InterPro, 26.5x), while the instance's own InterPro is "Actin family". Both are correct at their own level; the UI must show both and never let the cluster headline overwrite the instance fact.

units.name: Identifier typeahead
units.what_it_shows: Resolution of a typed gene symbol, RefSeq, ENSG or ENST to one transcript, with motif count and module badges per candidate.
units.encoding: Grouped rows by entity type; matched substring bolded; right-aligned motif count as a numeral plus a 40px bar against the corpus p99 (142); module colour dots.
units.data_source: Built at bake from /Users/wangyanz/.../data/processed/motif_full_annotations.parquet (gene_symbol, sequence_id) + /Users/wangyanz/Desktop/Project/sequence_design/data/GRCh37_latest_rna_sequence_pairs_long_transcript.parquet ('Gene stable ID','Transcript stable ID',refseq_id_without_ver). 17,847 symbols + 18,093 RefSeq + 20,481 ENSG + 20,481 ENST.
interactions: routes to excluded state when the symbol has no motifs
units.precompute_needed: Yes — one search_index.json, measured 1.71 MB raw / 0.42 MB gz.
units.why_it_earns_its_place: R1 begins with 'user searches'; without ID resolution the view is unreachable. ENSG/ENST map 1:1 to RefSeq in the search direction so no disambiguation UI is needed.

units.name: Transcript identity header
units.what_it_shows: Symbol, RefSeq, ENSG/ENST, the three region lengths, the true mRNA length, and per-region motif counts.
units.encoding: Two-row header; region lengths as chips in region colours (utr5 #E69F00, utr3 #A85A00, protein #0072B2); mRNA length computed as len(utr5)+len(cds)+len(utr3), never from transcript_length.
units.data_source: GRCh37_latest_rna_sequence_pairs_long_transcript.parquet (utr5_sequence, cds_sequence, utr3_sequence, protein_sequence) deduplicated on refseq_id_without_ver; counts from motif_full_annotations.parquet grouped by (sequence_id, region).
units.why_it_earns_its_place: Anchors every coordinate on the page and prevents the transcript_length trap I measured (ACTB 1,059 vs true 1,812).

units.name: Transcript-scale 5'UTR–CDS–3'UTR schematic
units.what_it_shows: The whole mRNA as one proportional bar with the three regions, the AUG and stop landmarks, and every motif as a tick — the orienting object before any zoom.
units.encoding: Single horizontal bar, segment widths exactly proportional to region length (ACTB 84 / 1,128 / 600), region fills; AUG and stop as vertical rules; motif ticks 2px in module colour beneath. Never draw the three regions at equal width — that is the commonest lie in this genre.
units.data_source: Region lengths from the sequence parquet; motif positions from motif_full_annotations.parquet (region, motif_start, motif_end) with protein motifs projected via utr5_len + 3*aa.
interactions: drag to set the detail viewport
hover a tick for a mini card
units.why_it_earns_its_place: The requirement asks explicitly for the transcript-scale overview; it is also the only place a reader sees that the 3'UTR is where 58% of all motifs live.

units.name: Unified mRNA coordinate axis (protein projected onto nucleotides)
units.what_it_shows: All three regions AND the protein motifs on one continuous nucleotide axis, so a protein motif and a UTR motif in the same transcript are spatially comparable for the first time.
units.encoding: One d3-scaleLinear from 0 to len(utr5)+len(cds)+len(utr3). Protein motif spans mapped as [utr5_len + 3*motif_start, utr5_len + 3*motif_end + 2]. A distinct hatch or outline marks projected (codon-derived) spans so they are never mistaken for directly-called nucleotide motifs.
units.data_source: Verified projection: cds_sequence length == 3*len(protein_sequence)+3 in 19,210/19,210 rows; checked against real ACTB codons (aa 23-27 DDAPR -> mRNA 153-167 -> GACGATGCCCCCCGG).
interactions: hover a projected span to see its codons
units.precompute_needed: No — arithmetic at render time from lengths already in the shard.
units.why_it_earns_its_place: This is the missing primitive. All four candidate designs drew three disconnected axes, which makes the paper's central bilingual claim un-showable in a single transcript. It is also free: the arithmetic is exact and verified.

units.name: In-transcript coupling arcs (protein motif × UTR motif)
units.what_it_shows: For THIS transcript, arcs joining a protein motif to a UTR motif whose clusters form a phylogenetically-gated pair — literally 'protein motif X pairs with UTR motif Y here'.
units.encoding: Bezier arcs below the motif lane on the unified axis. Arc thickness ~ phylo_corrected_score (range 0.146–1.769), colour by module, anchored at the highest-scoring instance of each cluster. Default top-8 by score; a count chip reads 'showing 8 of 33'.
units.data_source: phylo_corrected_candidates.csv (protein, utr, phylo_corrected_score, co_count, n_indep_clades, clade_concentration, frac_co_ZNF) intersected with this transcript's own cluster set from motif_full_annotations.parquet.
interactions: hover an arc for the four gate values
units.precompute_needed: Yes — per-transcript arc list; I measured mean 8.04 pairs/transcript, median 2, p90 23, max 203, 65.2% of transcripts have >=1.
units.prior_art: Arc/ribbon diagrams in RNA secondary structure viewers (R-chie, forna) and Circos link tracks.
units.why_it_earns_its_place: The single biggest gap in all four candidate designs. They relegate pairing to the network view, so the reader never sees the coupling in the gene they actually searched for. ACTB shows exactly 3 arcs, including the top-scoring pair in the entire analysis.

units.name: No-coupling state
units.what_it_shows: That 6,301 of 18,093 transcripts (34.8%) have zero co-present gated pairs, and why — their clusters' pairs did not survive the four-condition gate.
units.encoding: Inline muted card in the arc lane's vertical space, stating the count and the gate, with a one-click switch to the suggestive tier (which lifts coverage to 92.3%).
units.data_source: Computed absence against phylo_corrected_candidates.csv; gate wording verbatim from .../03.interacting_modules/MODULES_REPORT.md.
units.why_it_earns_its_place: A third of transcripts hit this. Silently drawing nothing would read as a rendering bug rather than the real scientific result it is.

units.name: Codon bridge — protein motif to its encoding nucleotides
units.what_it_shows: The exact CDS nucleotides that encode a selected protein motif, shown as triplets under the amino acids.
units.encoding: Monospace codon row aligned 3:1 under the amino-acid row, motif codons tinted, reading-frame positions 1/2/3 marked with a repeating tick.
units.data_source: cds_sequence[3*motif_start : 3*motif_end+3] from the sequence parquet; verified exact on ACTB's four protein motifs.
interactions: jump to those coordinates on the unified axis
units.why_it_earns_its_place: Makes the bilingual claim physical rather than metaphorical, and is the only way a reader can check that a protein motif and a UTR motif are on the same molecule.

units.name: Reading-frame / codon ruler
units.what_it_shows: Codon boundaries and frame across the CDS portion of the unified axis.
units.encoding: Repeating 1-2-3 tick pattern; major ticks every 10 codons; amino-acid index on a secondary scale.
units.data_source: Derived from len(utr5) and len(cds); no new data.
interactions: toggle nt vs codon vs aa numbering
units.why_it_earns_its_place: Without it the unified axis silently mixes a 1-nt and a 3-nt quantum and readers will mis-measure protein motif lengths.

units.name: 5'UTR NTScore track
units.what_it_shows: The model's per-nucleotide conditional log-probability along the 5'UTR — the manuscript's central quantity, at full resolution.
units.encoding: Filled area, x = position, y = NTScore on a FIXED domain [-8, 0] for cross-transcript comparability, with a dashed rule at the region mean (SeqScore) and a zero rule. Optional per-transcript autoscale, clearly labelled.
units.data_source: /Users/wangyanz/Desktop/Project/sequence_design/explore_biology/01.protein_localization/analysis/data/h5cache/outputs_utr5_score_0326.h5, group <refseq>/score. I verified: 18,093 keys, exactly 1:1 with the motif transcript set, array length == len(utr5_sequence) in 18,093/18,093, observed min -7.281, max -0.002. ACTB: 84 values, SeqScore -0.8708.
interactions: brush to zoom (drives the sequence pane)
units.precompute_needed: No if a server reads the h5 (measured 0.202 ms/transcript); yes if static — quantize to uint8 over [-8,0] per transcript.
units.why_it_earns_its_place: This is what makes the view a scientific instrument rather than coloured text; it is the reason a reader believes a highlighted stretch was called for a reason.

units.name: 3'UTR NTScore track
units.what_it_shows: Same for the 3'UTR, where the ARE/ELAVL1 biology lives and where 58% of motifs are.
units.encoding: As utr5_ntscore; for regions over ~2,000 nt (p99 6,008, max 7,601) min/max decimate to two points per pixel column so peaks survive downsampling — never mean-downsample a score track.
units.data_source: /Users/wangyanz/Desktop/Project/sequence_design/data/outputs_utr3_score_0318.h5, group <refseq>/score. Verified 18,093/18,093 present and length-aligned for the portal universe; observed min -7.688. ACTB: 600 values, SeqScore -1.1648. NOTE: the file holds 18,585 keys and some of the 492 extras are length-mismatched — restrict to the motif universe.
units.why_it_earns_its_place: Same as utr5; also the only track that can be visually compared against CLIP peaks to support the paper's ELAVL1 argument.

units.name: Explicit 'no score computed' band over the CDS
units.what_it_shows: That NTScore exists for 5'UTR and 3'UTR only — there is no CDS or per-residue protein score anywhere in the project.
units.encoding: A hatched, desaturated band occupying the score lane's full height across the CDS span, labelled 'no per-nucleotide score computed for CDS'. Critically NOT a flat line at zero and NOT a gap.
units.data_source: Absence of any CDS/protein score file; confirmed across the inventory.
interactions: hover for the one-line explanation and a link to methods
units.why_it_earns_its_place: On a unified axis a gap reads as 'score = 0' or 'nothing here'. A flat line would be an outright fabrication. This is the honest mark for missing data and it costs nothing.

units.name: Per-motif pLDDT track (protein)
units.what_it_shows: AlphaFold local confidence for each protein motif — the substitute for the score track the protein panel cannot have, and the ordered-domain vs IDR axis behind the M1/M5 disorder story.
units.encoding: Step bars, one per protein motif at its span, y on a FIXED 0–1 domain (measured min 0.1, median 0.8, max 1.0 — NOT the 0–100 AlphaFold convention), reference rules at 0.5 and 0.7. Labelled 'per motif, not per residue' and never drawn in the same visual idiom as NTScore.
units.data_source: motif_full_annotations.parquet column plddt (254,466 non-null, protein rows only; null on all UTR rows).
interactions: hover for value and confidence band
units.why_it_earns_its_place: Without it the protein half of R1 has no quantitative layer at all. The 0–1 scale detail matters: treating it as 0–100 would render every protein motif as 'very low confidence'.

units.name: Single-lane motif span layer
units.what_it_shows: Every called motif on the transcript as a discrete positioned block.
units.encoding: One rect per motif, x from motif_start to motif_end+1 (0-based, both ends inclusive), fill = module colour with grey #A7A7A7 for the 45.3% of instances in unassigned clusters, opacity ramped by motif_score. A 1px inset outline plus a 1px gap so the 53,729 exactly-abutting adjacent pairs (9,838 of them same-cluster) never fuse into one false motif.
units.data_source: motif_full_annotations.parquet (sequence_id, region, motif_start, motif_end, motif_cluster, motif_score).
units.why_it_earns_its_place: The core mark of the whole view. One lane is provably sufficient: max stacking depth is exactly 1 across all 53,367 (transcript, region) groups, and projected protein motifs occupy CDS coordinates disjoint from UTR motifs.

units.name: Interval lane packer (annotation tracks only)
units.what_it_shows: Overlapping annotation intervals stacked into the minimum number of non-overlapping rows.
units.encoding: Greedy sweep-line row assignment; row count printed in the lane header so a 6-row UniProt lane is understood as density, not noise.
units.data_source: Applies to InterPro domains (median 5, max 436 per transcript), UniProt features, and the 4 CLIP method lanes — all of which genuinely overlap. Deliberately NOT applied to the motif layer.
interactions: collapse a packed lane to a single density strip
units.why_it_earns_its_place: The brief asks about multi-lane layout for overlapping motifs; the honest answer is that motifs never overlap but annotations do, so the packer belongs here and nowhere else.

units.name: Wrapped sequence pane with in-place highlights
units.what_it_shows: The actual residues, 60 per line, with motifs highlighted as real text — the literal wording of R1.
units.encoding: Monospace 13px/1.75, 10-character groups, flat run-length alternation of plain text nodes and bordered motif spans. Background tint = module colour at ~18% alpha, border = region colour. Measured worst case 381 elements for all three regions on one page (median 89), so plain DOM is comfortable.
units.data_source: Sequences from the deduplicated GRCh37 parquet; spans sliced seq[motif_start : motif_end+1] — the verified contract, exact for 889,215/889,215 rows.
interactions: select text (reports length, GC%, covered motifs)
units.why_it_earns_its_place: Must be DOM, not canvas: a wet-lab reader's first action is to select and copy a sequence. Canvas would render faster and destroy the primary use case.

units.name: Track mode for long regions
units.what_it_shows: The whole region as geometry when it is too long to read (3'UTR p99 6,008 nt, max 7,601).
units.encoding: Motif rects + score track on a compressed axis, letters appearing only past ~1.5 px/nt; the mode switch is automatic by default (5'UTR reads, 3'UTR tracks) and manually overridable.
units.data_source: Same as seq_pane_read.
units.why_it_earns_its_place: Rendering 7,601 characters of readable text is useless; rendering geometry for an 84-nt 5'UTR is equally useless. The view needs both and must pick sensibly.

units.name: Per-line NTScore sparkline
units.what_it_shows: The score for exactly the 60 nucleotides on the line beneath it, keeping score and letters aligned in read mode.
units.encoding: 60-cell micro bar strip in the left gutter, sharing the [-8,0] scale and colour ramp with the main track.
units.data_source: The same h5 arrays, sliced per line.
interactions: hover a cell for base + score
click to select the containing motif
units.why_it_earns_its_place: In read mode the main score track scrolls out of alignment with the text; this keeps the model's evidence adjacent to the residues it refers to.

units.name: Coordinate gutter
units.what_it_shows: 1-based position at the start of each sequence line.
units.encoding: Right-aligned muted monospace numerals in a fixed-width gutter; amino-acid index for the protein pane.
units.data_source: Derived from sequence length.
interactions: click a number to copy that coordinate
units.why_it_earns_its_place: A sequence view without coordinates cannot be cross-referenced with any other tool the reader uses.

units.name: 3'UTR coordinate origin toggle
units.what_it_shows: 3'UTR positions numbered from the stop codon (biologically meaningful) or from the region start (matches the stored data).
units.encoding: Two-state control; the active convention is printed in the ruler header, never implicit.
units.data_source: Region offsets from the sequence parquet.
interactions: toggle; the choice propagates to tooltips, the table and exports
units.why_it_earns_its_place: The isoform and ARE literature numbers 3'UTR positions from the stop codon; without the toggle every coordinate a reader quotes will be off by len(utr5)+len(cds).

units.name: RNA/DNA alphabet toggle
units.what_it_shows: UTR sequences and motif strings as RNA (U) to match the manuscript, or as the stored DNA alphabet.
units.encoding: Two-state control, RNA default. Applies to 5'UTR and 3'UTR only and NEVER to the protein pane, where U is selenocysteine.
units.data_source: Storage is DNA-only (verified: UTR alphabets are A/C/G/T with zero U). ACTB's utr5_0004 motif CGAGACCGCGT displays as CGAGACCGCGU.
interactions: search accepts both forms and normalises to T before matching
units.why_it_earns_its_place: The manuscript writes every RNA motif in RNA alphabet (UCAUC, UCUCC, GCCACC). Without transliteration the portal literally cannot display the motifs the paper names, and a reader typing UCUCC gets zero hits.

units.name: Region minimap with viewport brush
units.what_it_shows: The whole region compressed with motif density and a coarse score silhouette, plus a draggable viewport rectangle.
units.encoding: 20px strip: 2px motif ticks in module colour over a compressed score silhouette; translucent viewport rect.
units.data_source: Same motif and score arrays, downsampled at render.
units.why_it_earns_its_place: The only workable navigation for the 587 transcripts with 3'UTRs >= 5,000 nt; without it a reader zoomed to 60 nt is lost in a 7,601-nt region.

units.name: Motif density histogram
units.what_it_shows: Where motifs bunch along each region for this transcript.
units.encoding: 20-bin bar strip under the region header, bars tinted by the dominant module in each bin.
units.data_source: Computed client-side from the loaded motif_start/motif_end array and region length.
interactions: click a bin to scroll the viewport there
units.why_it_earns_its_place: Gives a shape to a dense 3'UTR (up to 182 motifs) that a flat lane of rects cannot convey at overview zoom.

units.name: Region motif-coverage bar
units.what_it_shows: What fraction of the region's bases sit inside a motif, against the corpus median.
units.encoding: Thin bar with a tick at the corpus median (utr5 0.307, utr3 0.261, protein 0.288) so the value is comparative, not absolute.
units.data_source: Computed from motif_start/motif_end; corpus medians precomputed once from motif_full_annotations.parquet.
interactions: hover for exact fraction and percentile
units.why_it_earns_its_place: Roughly a quarter to a third of every region is highlighted; stating that number up front stops a reader concluding the highlighting is meaningless noise.

units.name: SeqScore tile per region
units.what_it_shows: The region's mean NTScore — the manuscript's SeqScore — positioned within the corpus distribution.
units.encoding: Small tile: value plus a marker inside a corpus density strip for that region.
units.data_source: Mean of the h5 score array (ACTB utr5 -0.8708, utr3 -1.1648); corpus distributions precomputed over all 18,093.
units.why_it_earns_its_place: SeqScore is a named quantity in the paper and is free to compute; the corpus context is what makes a single negative number interpretable.

units.name: UTR composition sparkline
units.what_it_shows: Local GC / AU content along each UTR in a sliding window.
units.encoding: Thin line in the track stack, 50-nt window; labelled as sequence composition, not model output.
units.data_source: Computed from utr5_sequence / utr3_sequence.
units.why_it_earns_its_place: Makes the M1 AU-rich vs M2 GC-rich distinction (cluster mean GC 0.344 vs 0.497) checkable in the reader's own gene instead of taken on faith.

units.name: Kozak context inset
units.what_it_shows: The last ~12 nt of the 5'UTR plus the first codons around the AUG, with the -3 and +4 positions marked.
units.encoding: Small monospace inset pinned at the AUG landmark; -3 purine and +4 G called out.
units.data_source: utr5_sequence tail + cds_sequence head; classification vocabulary from .../examples_of_each_gene/M6_utr5_0004_GCCGCCACC_kozak_genes.csv (gene, kozak_bits, minus3_nt, minus3_purine, kozak_context, class) for the 372 genes it covers.
interactions: hover for the Kozak class where the gene is in the 372-gene panel
units.why_it_earns_its_place: M6's whole story is that utr5_0004 rediscovers the Kozak sequence; showing the actual context at the actual AUG is the most direct possible evidence, and ACTB is an M6 example.

units.name: Poly(A) signal literal marker
units.what_it_shows: Occurrences of AATAAA/ATTAAA in the 3'UTR.
units.encoding: Small diamond markers on a thin lane, explicitly labelled 'literal string match, not a model call' and visually distinct from motif rects.
units.data_source: Literal scan of utr3_sequence; no stored source.
interactions: hover for the matched hexamer and position
units.why_it_earns_its_place: Orients a reader at the 3' end at near-zero cost — but only if it is unmistakably marked as a regex hit rather than a MIRTO output, or it will be mistaken for a discovered motif.

units.name: CLIP evidence lanes, one per method
units.what_it_shows: Which RBPs annotate each UTR motif, kept in four separate method lanes rather than merged.
units.encoding: Four lanes (eCLIP / PAR-CLIP,PARalyzer / iCLIP,Piranha / iCLIP,CIMS); each hit a labelled tick under its motif; lane header carries the method's corpus coverage.
units.data_source: motif_full_annotations.parquet list columns RBPs_eCLIP, 'RBPs_PAR-CLIP,PARalyzer', 'RBPs_iCLIP,Piranha_0.01', 'RBPs_iCLIP,CIMS'. ACTB's 45-nt AU-rich 3'UTR element carries DDX55, NKRF, SUB1, TIAL1.
interactions: click an RBP to filter the page
units.why_it_earns_its_place: Only 4 of 203 RBP names appear in all four methods and 166 appear in exactly one; merging them into a single 'RBP' field would erase the method structure that is the honest confidence signal. Follows POSTAR3's stacked-by-method convention.

units.name: CLIP peak evidence drawer
units.what_it_shows: The actual peaks behind an RBP chip: how many, from which cell lines, at what scores.
units.encoding: Table plus a small cell-line bar chart; peak_id shown verbatim for traceability.
units.data_source: /Users/wangyanz/.../data/processed/00.eclip/motif_rbp_overlaps.parquet — 2,671,559 rows, columns raw_motif_index, peak_id, RBP_name, score, sample, method, Chromosome/Start/End/Strand (verified schema). 325,996 distinct motifs, mean 8.2 peaks each, 19 cell lines.

units.why_it_earns_its_place: Turns 'TIAL1' from a label into evidence a reader can weigh, and enables a cell-line filter no static figure can offer.

units.name: RBP method-agreement badge
units.what_it_shows: How many of the four CLIP methods support a given call.
units.encoding: Four small squares [e][P][i][C], filled per supporting method, with '3 of 4' in text.
units.data_source: The four RBP list columns. Measured distribution over 634,749 UTR motifs: 0 methods 308,753 / 1 144,288 / 2 95,096 / 3 57,474 / 4 29,138.
interactions: hover for which RBPs came from which method
units.why_it_earns_its_place: A free, honest confidence axis that also explains why PAR-CLIP-only RBPs (ATXN2 115,724, ELAVL1 93,426) dominate raw counts.

units.name: RBP nomenclature note
units.what_it_shows: That RBP names are raw POSTAR3 labels and are not normalised.
units.encoding: Small info affordance on the RBP lane header listing the known collisions.

units.what_it_shows: Where each UTR motif sits on GRCh37, including exon-split blocks.

units.name: InterPro domain ruler
units.what_it_shows: The protein's real domains with true coordinates, so a reader sees whether a motif falls inside a domain or in a linker.

interactions: hover for IPR accession, type and GO
units.why_it_earns_its_place: 'Motif sits inside the Actin family domain' is the single most useful protein-side statement the view can make, and ACTB demonstrates it directly.

units.name: Typed UniProt feature track
units.what_it_shows: Chain, Domain, Region, Helix, Beta strand, Transmembrane, Signal and Modified residue features under the protein — including the structural ones the shipped comma-joined column silently dropped.

units.what_it_shows: MobiDB disorder, LIP and phase-separation regions as actual residue intervals under the protein sequence — not just a list of 87 term names.

units.data_source: /Users/wangyanz/.../data/raw_annotations/06.mobidb/mobidb_search_2026-05-13T19-55-12.tsv — verified structure: UniProt acc, term, comma-joined 'start..end' ranges (e.g. '1..2,71..75,233..246'), content_fraction, content_count, protein length. Read with header=None.
interactions: hover for the term and its provenance

units.why_it_earns_its_place: The IDR narrative (M1, M5, prot_0072 phase separation) is currently only assertable at cluster level. This makes it visible in the reader's own protein, and it pairs naturally with the pLDDT track.

units.name: Signal peptide / transmembrane marker
units.what_it_shows: The N-terminal signal peptide and any transmembrane segments — the M3 secretory story.
units.encoding: Distinct N-terminal cap glyph plus TM segment blocks on the protein axis.
units.data_source: Prefer UniProt 'Signal' features from uniprot_annotation.parquet (2,366 protein motifs, 7.9x more than the shipped column). The signalp_annotation column covers only 298 motifs (0.117%) and was derived from the SignalP 6.0 TRAINING SET, not from running SignalP — label it accurately if shown at all.
units.why_it_earns_its_place: M3's claim is Leu-rich signal peptide x GC-rich 5'UTR; the marker makes that checkable in RET/VEGFB/TIMP3. But the shipped SignalP column is close to useless and must not be presented as a SignalP prediction.

units.name: ELM short linear motif marker
units.what_it_shows: Overlapping ELM functional sites on the protein.
units.encoding: Small labelled ticks; sparse by nature (797 motifs, 0.313% of protein motifs).
units.data_source: Re-join .../data/raw_annotations/02.elm/elm_instances.tsv (4,277 instances: Primary_Acc, Start, End, ELMIdentifier, Accession, References) + elm_classes.tsv (353 classes with Regex, Probability). The master table keeps only FunctionalSiteName, and 69 of 206 site names map to 2–10 classes, so text->accession is ambiguous.

units.why_it_earns_its_place: Rare but the most mechanistically interpretable protein annotation available; worth doing properly or not at all.

units.name: Motif instance inspector
units.what_it_shows: The full record of one clicked motif: sequence in both alphabets, coordinates, length, cluster, module, scores, and every annotation.
units.encoding: Sticky side panel (never a modal, never inline — the sequence must not reflow); sectioned card stack with the motif sequence in monospace flanked by 8–10 greyed context residues.
units.data_source: motif_full_annotations.parquet row by raw_motif_index plus the per-transcript annotation shard.
units.why_it_earns_its_place: 'Click detail' is an explicit requirement; a side panel rather than a modal is what lets a reader keep their place in a 7,601-nt sequence.

units.name: Annotation chips with provenance
units.what_it_shows: Each annotation as a chip carrying its database, the overlap rule used, and a deep link.
units.encoding: Chip groups per source, tinted by layer (RNA #2E7D9A, protein #9C6B1E), with a superscript rule marker: 'ov' = motif overlaps feature (InterPro/UniProt/ELM), 'in' = motif contained in region (MobiDB/IDPO).
units.data_source: The 11 annotation columns of motif_full_annotations.parquet, MASKED by the `applies` field of /Users/wangyanz/Desktop/Project/sequence_design/sequence_annotation/annotation_coverage_stats.json. InterPro chips from .../01.interpro/motif_interpro_annotations.parquet (overlapping_interpro_labels) + interpro_entry_map.csv — never by comma-splitting, which is wrong for 41.34% of annotated protein motifs.
interactions: hover for source, rule and corpus coverage
click for an external deep link
units.why_it_earns_its_place: Different databases used different overlap semantics and the master table documents none of them; a chip without its rule is an unfalsifiable claim.

units.name: Annotation region mask (build-time guard)
units.what_it_shows: Nothing visible — it is the guard that prevents a visible scientific error.
units.encoding: n/a; enforced in the data layer and asserted in CI.
units.data_source: MobiDB is populated on 67.0% of 5'UTR and 25.3% of 3'UTR rows with protein-disorder terms (209,959 spurious rows), plus IDPO 1,825 and SignalP 665, because those builders never filtered region=='protein'. The `applies` field in annotation_coverage_stats.json is the correct rule and reproduces all 8 published coverage numbers exactly.
interactions: build fails loudly if the mask regresses
units.why_it_earns_its_place: Without it the portal tells an RNA biologist that a 3'UTR nucleotide motif has intrinsic protein disorder, on two-thirds of 5'UTR motifs. This is the single highest-embarrassment defect available in R1.

units.name: Cluster mini-card in the inspector
units.what_it_shows: The selected motif's cluster at a glance: mini logo or fallback, consensus, size, module.
units.encoding: 80px logo + one-line auto-name + instance/gene counts + module chip.
units.data_source: .../intermediate/consensus_repertoire.pkl PWMs (451 of 900 clusters), consensus_meta.csv (cid, consensus, coverage, carriers), plus a per-cluster index.
interactions: click through to the cluster page
hover a logo column for probabilities
units.why_it_earns_its_place: The R1→R2 handoff. A reader who clicks a highlight wants to know what family it belongs to without a page load.

units.name: Consensus coverage honesty badge
units.what_it_shows: How much of its own cluster a consensus actually explains, next to any logo shown in R1.
units.encoding: Coverage bar plus the carrier count; below ~0.35 the logo is visually de-emphasised and captioned 'describes 21% of this cluster's instances — not necessarily this site'.
units.data_source: consensus_meta.csv columns coverage (median 0.365) and carriers. Worked example: utr5_0004#0 CGCCGCCACC has coverage 0.212 over only 51 carriers — yet ACTB's 5'UTR motifs are in utr5_0004.
interactions: hover for the definition (fraction matched at >=0.5 bits/position)
units.why_it_earns_its_place: This is the specific misleading unit the brief warns about. A PWM logo beside a highlighted span reads as 'this is the site found in your gene'. At coverage 0.212 that is false, and ACTB — the default landing gene — is exactly such a case.

units.name: Cluster-label vs instance-annotation disagreement flag
units.what_it_shows: When the cluster's headline enrichment label contradicts the instance's own annotation.
units.encoding: Both shown, stacked and labelled by level: 'this instance: Actin family (InterPro)' above 'this cluster overall: Histone-fold, 26.5x'. A small divergence marker when they disagree.
units.data_source: Instance InterPro from motif_interpro_annotations.parquet; cluster label from cluster_term_labels.csv / cluster_term_enrichment.csv.gz. Real case: ACTB's protein motifs are prot_0040, cluster label 'Histone-fold', instance annotation 'ATPase, nucleotide binding domain, Actin family'.
interactions: hover for what each level means
units.why_it_earns_its_place: Occurs on the default landing gene. Letting a gene-level enrichment label overwrite a residue-level fact is exactly how a portal loses expert trust in one screenshot.

units.name: Instance score percentile meters
units.what_it_shows: Where this instance's motif_score, motif_entropy and pLDDT sit in the corpus and in its own cluster.
units.encoding: Three thin bullet charts: corpus density strip, cluster median tick, instance marker, percentile printed. motif_score domain is negative (min -4.831, median -1.135, max ~0).
units.data_source: Instance values from motif_full_annotations.parquet; corpus and per-cluster quantiles precomputed.
interactions: hover for exact value and percentile
units.why_it_earns_its_place: A bare 'score -0.94' is uninterpretable; the same number as a percentile against its own cluster is actionable.

units.name: Tooltip mini-histogram: position within cluster
units.what_it_shows: Where this instance's relative position falls inside its cluster's own 20-bin positional distribution.
units.encoding: 20-bar micro histogram inside the tooltip with this instance's bin highlighted and the cluster median marked.
units.data_source: Per-cluster positional histograms computed for all 900 clusters as relpos=(motif_start+motif_end)/2/region_length (join verified 18,093/18,093, 0 out-of-range); validated against the 142 published pos_hist arrays in streme_pos_cache_all6.pkl.
units.why_it_earns_its_place: Answers 'is this instance typical of its cluster?' in the hover, which is how a reader judges whether a cap-proximal cluster call actually applies here.

units.name: Tooltip mini-histogram: score in cluster
units.what_it_shows: This instance's motif_score against its cluster's score distribution.
units.encoding: Micro density strip with a marker; shares the negative domain with the main score encoding.
units.data_source: motif_full_annotations.parquet motif_score grouped by motif_cluster.
units.why_it_earns_its_place: Distinguishes a strong exemplar from a marginal cluster member without opening the cluster page.

units.name: Motif hover card
units.what_it_shows: Coordinates, sequence, cluster, module, score and top annotation without a click.
units.encoding: Compact dark card anchored to the span, containing the two mini-histograms above.
units.data_source: The loaded transcript payload plus its annotation shard.
units.why_it_earns_its_place: With a median of 43 motifs per transcript, clicking each one to identify it is unusable; hover is the primary triage interaction.

units.name: Transcript module fingerprint
units.what_it_shows: How this transcript's motifs distribute across M1–M6 and 'no module'.
units.encoding: Single stacked horizontal bar in module colours with an explicitly hatched grey 'no module' segment and counts on hover.
units.data_source: motif_cluster mapped through modules.json (513 of 900 clusters assigned). SOX2 reads 43 M1 / 3 M2 / rest unassigned; ACTB carries M6 and M1.
interactions: click a segment to filter the tracks
click through to the module page
units.why_it_earns_its_place: The R1→R3 bridge, and the honest place to show that 45.3% of motif instances belong to no module at all.

units.name: Annotation availability strip
units.what_it_shows: Which panels can be populated for this transcript, before the reader scrolls into an empty one.
units.encoding: Row of pill badges, filled = available, outlined = absent with the reason and the corpus fraction on hover.
units.data_source: Precomputed flags: UniProt accession 16,911/18,093 (idmapping_2026_05_08.tsv); InterPro domain track 13,941/18,093 (annotated_protein_sequences.csv); UTR genome coordinates all 634,749 UTR motifs; module membership 8,846/18,093 (module_gene_index.csv refseq_ids); NTScore both regions 18,093/18,093.
interactions: hover for 'InterPro coordinates exist for 13,941 of 18,093 transcripts; this one is not among them'
units.why_it_earns_its_place: Converts four different kinds of missing data from apparent bugs into stated coverage limits, which is the difference between a resource and a broken page.

units.name: Empty state: transcript has no motifs
units.what_it_shows: Why a searched gene returns nothing — for 1,117 of 19,210 RefSeq transcripts.
units.encoding: Card naming the gene, its true mRNA length, and how that compares to motif-bearing transcripts, with a length bar.
units.data_source: Set difference of the sequence parquet against the 18,093 motif transcripts. MEASURED, and this corrects the surveys: the real mRNA length (utr5+cds+utr3) of motif-bearing transcripts is median 2,923 / p99 8,736 / max 11,426; motif-free is median 10,749 / max 109,224 (TTN). 445 transcripts exceed 11,426 and all lack motifs, but 672 under it also lack motifs.
interactions: suggest another transcript of the same gene if one exists
units.why_it_earns_its_place: Searching TTN is the first thing a sceptical reader does. The message must NOT quote '7,784 nt context cap' — that number came from the transcript_length column, which I verified is not the mRNA length (ACTB 1,059 vs true 1,812).

units.name: Empty state: symbol not resolvable
units.what_it_shows: The difference between a typo, an alias, and a genuinely excluded gene.
units.encoding: Card with fuzzy symbol suggestions (trigram over the 17,847 symbols) and a distinct branch when the RefSeq exists but carries no motifs.
units.data_source: Search index; note that the sequence parquet has no gene_symbol column, so the 1,117 motif-free transcripts cannot be labelled from local data alone.
units.precompute_needed: Yes, partially — recovering symbols for the excluded set needs an external RefSeq→symbol map (NCBI gene2refseq or one offline mygene call for 1,117 ids, ~30 KB JSON). Not derivable from files on disk.
units.why_it_earns_its_place: Without it 'TTN' and 'TNT' fail identically, which reads as a broken search rather than a scoped corpus.

units.name: Empty state: region has no motifs
units.what_it_shows: That 902 transcripts are missing at least one track (808 no 5'UTR motifs, 87 no 3'UTR, 17 no protein).
units.encoding: The sequence renders normally with zero highlights plus a muted inline note; the panel is never hidden.
units.data_source: Absence of rows for that (sequence_id, region) in motif_full_annotations.parquet.
units.why_it_earns_its_place: Hiding the panel would make a real biological/analytical absence indistinguishable from a layout failure.

units.name: 'No annotation' state per source
units.what_it_shows: That 36.1% of motif instances carry no annotation at all, and which source is empty here.
units.encoding: Greyed 'none' chip in the source's row rather than a hidden row, with the source's corpus coverage on hover.
units.data_source: annotation_coverage_stats.json per-source coverage with correct denominators.
units.why_it_earns_its_place: A hidden row implies the source was never consulted; a greyed row states it was consulted and found nothing, which is a different and true claim.

units.name: Motif filter chips and score slider
units.what_it_shows: Density control over a page carrying a median of 43 and up to 189 motifs.
units.encoding: Chip row (region, module, annotated-only, cluster, coupled-only) plus a two-handle motif_score range slider with this transcript's score histogram behind the track; a live 'showing 17 of 20' count.
units.data_source: The loaded transcript payload.
interactions: filters DIM to ~25% opacity rather than removing spans, so coordinates never shift
units.why_it_earns_its_place: Filtering by removal would reflow the sequence and misrepresent density; dimming preserves the true picture while directing attention.

units.name: 'Only coupled motifs' filter
units.what_it_shows: Just the motifs that participate in a gated pair within this transcript.
units.encoding: Single toggle; when on, uncoupled motifs dim and the arc layer becomes the focus; count printed.
units.data_source: The precomputed per-transcript arc list.
units.why_it_earns_its_place: Reduces a 43-motif page to the handful that carry the paper's actual claim — median 2 pairs per transcript.

units.name: Linked selection across representations
units.what_it_shows: That the overview tick, the ribbon rect, the sequence span and the table row are the same object.

units.data_source: raw_motif_index as the single identity key (unique, 0..889,214).
units.why_it_earns_its_place: The brief names selection linking explicitly; without a single identity key the four views drift and the page feels like four unrelated widgets.

units.name: Linked brush / zoom coupling
units.what_it_shows: One viewport shared by the overview, the score track, the sequence pane and the annotation lanes.
units.encoding: A single [start, end] range in shared state; every track derives its scale from it.
units.data_source: n/a — interaction state.
interactions: zoom to a selected motif with padding
units.why_it_earns_its_place: Independent zoom per track is the classic genome-browser failure; alignment across lanes is the entire value of a stacked layout.

units.name: All-motifs table
units.what_it_shows: Every motif on the transcript as sortable, filterable, exportable rows.
units.encoding: Dense table: region, start, end, length, sequence (RNA for UTRs), cluster, cluster name, module, motif_score, entropy, pLDDT, annotation count; region colour as a left rule; inline data bars on numeric columns.
units.data_source: motif_full_annotations.parquet rows for this sequence_id plus the annotation shard.
interactions: CSV export of the filtered view
units.why_it_earns_its_place: Per-transcript counts are bounded (median 43, max 189) so no virtualisation is needed, and the table is the accessible, sortable, exportable equivalent of the graphical layer.

units.name: Coupled-pairs table for this transcript
units.what_it_shows: The gated pairs present here with their four gate values, as the tabular twin of the arc layer.
units.encoding: Rows: protein cluster, UTR cluster, phylo_corrected_score, co_count, n_indep_clades, clade_concentration, frac_co_ZNF, module; sorted by phylo_corrected_score by default.
units.data_source: phylo_corrected_candidates.csv intersected with this transcript's clusters.
interactions: hover to highlight the corresponding arc
click to open the pair page
units.why_it_earns_its_place: Arcs are good for gestalt and bad for reading numbers; the gate values must be legible somewhere, and never behind a hover only.

units.name: Four-condition gate gauges (inline)
units.what_it_shows: For any coupling shown in R1, each gate value against its threshold rather than a pass/fail boolean.
units.encoding: Four micro bullet charts: clade_concentration < 0.35, n_indep_clades >= 8, npmi_mip_APC > 0.10, co_count >= 10, plus frac_co_ZNF as a read-only artifact bar on a 0–0.5 scale.
units.data_source: phylo_corrected_candidates.csv. ACTB's prot_0040 x utr5_0004: score 1.7694, npmi 0.628, co_count 175, 23 clades, frac_co_ZNF 0.000.
interactions: hover for the condition verbatim from MODULES_REPORT.md
units.why_it_earns_its_place: Any coupling shown in a gene view will be read as an interaction. Putting the evidence inline — not behind a details toggle — is what makes the claim honest at the point of reading.

units.name: Coupling caveat, inline at the arc layer
units.what_it_shows: That an arc is co-occurrence of motif clusters across genes, not a demonstrated physical interaction in this molecule.
units.encoding: One-line label attached to the arc lane header, not a page-level banner that users learn to ignore.
units.data_source: Verbatim from .../module_gene_members/README.md and MODULES_REPORT.md.
units.why_it_earns_its_place: The arc layer is the one unit in R1 that could be catastrophically over-read. An arc drawn inside a single transcript especially invites 'these two bind each other in this mRNA', which the data cannot support: the evidence is cross-gene co-occurrence.

units.name: 'Why is this highlighted?' explainer
units.what_it_shows: How a motif was called — delta-attention peaks intersected with high NTScore — and that the underlying attention matrices are not stored.
units.encoding: Short explainer in the inspector with a link to methods; the pipeline figure is explicitly labelled schematic.
units.data_source: Manuscript Methods; PANELS.md states Fig 3a is drawn from synthetic data and no attention matrices exist on disk.
units.why_it_earns_its_place: It is the first question every reader has about a highlight. Answering it honestly — including that the attribution itself cannot be shown — is better than leaving them to assume the highlight is a database hit.

units.name: Encoding legend
units.what_it_shows: What every fill, border, shape and opacity means, including the coordinate convention.
units.encoding: Compact panel with live swatches drawn by the same code as the tracks; states 'coordinates are 0-based, inclusive of both ends' and 'fill = module, grey = no module; cluster identity is in labels, not colour'.

interactions: click a module swatch to filter
units.why_it_earns_its_place: Three simultaneous encodings (module fill, region border, score opacity) are unreadable without a key, and the legend is where the 'colour is not cluster' rule gets stated.

units.name: Cluster identity encoding policy
units.what_it_shows: Not a chart — the rule that cluster identity is carried by label, position and selection, never by hue.

units.data_source: MEASURED: distinct motif_clusters per transcript median 26, p90 55, p99 80, max 108; only 13.7% of transcripts have <=12. A categorical palette cannot resolve 26 classes.
interactions: click a cluster name anywhere to accent all its instances
units.why_it_earns_its_place: Three of the four candidate designs offered 'color by: cluster' as a first-class option. At a median of 26 clusters per transcript that produces an unreadable rainbow and implies distinctions the eye cannot make. This unit is the corrective.

units.name: Per-character residue colouring
units.what_it_shows: Nucleotide and amino-acid identity as an optional character-level channel.
units.encoding: NT_COLORS A #009E73, C #0072B2, G #E69F00, U/T #D55E00; amino acids by the examples_lib aacol scheme (L #C1121F, hydrophobic #E8862E, polar #2A9D8F, charged #3557A6). OFF by default — with ~30% of characters already highlighted, per-character colour plus motif tint is unreadable.

interactions: applies within motifs only, or everywhere
units.why_it_earns_its_place: Matches the manuscript figures and helps at high zoom, but defaulting it on would collide with the motif tint — the honest default is off.

units.name: Hierarchy breadcrumb
units.what_it_shows: Where the reader is: ACTB / 5'UTR / nt 5-15 / utr5_0004 / M6.
units.encoding: Chips with region and module colours.
units.data_source: Router state plus the cluster index.
interactions: each chip navigates up a level
units.why_it_earns_its_place: The instance→cluster→module hierarchy is four levels deep and easy to get lost in; the breadcrumb is also where the current resolution level is stated.

units.name: Multi-transcript picker
units.what_it_shows: The alternative transcripts of the 215 genes (1.20%) that have more than one, with lengths and motif counts.
units.encoding: Dropdown showing RefSeq, region lengths and motif count; a static label for the 17,632 single-transcript genes.
units.data_source: motif_full_annotations.parquet grouped by gene_symbol over sequence_id; distribution {1:17632, 2:193, 3:17, 4:3, 5:1, 7:1}, max 7 (BAG6).
interactions: select to navigate, preserving region and zoom
units.why_it_earns_its_place: Keying the page on gene_symbol and taking the first sequence_id silently mis-slices these genes — APEX1's two transcripts have 5'UTRs of 232 and 237 nt, so coordinates from one address the other. The page must be keyed on sequence_id.

units.name: Isoform scope note
units.what_it_shows: That the motifome is one transcript per gene, so this page is not an isoform browser.
units.encoding: One line in the header stating which RefSeq is shown and that alternative UTR isoforms are not indexed.
units.data_source: 18,093 transcripts over 17,847 symbols.
interactions: link to the isoform case study where one exists
units.why_it_earns_its_place: Prevents a reader concluding that CD47's short 3'UTR isoform has no motifs, when in fact it was never analysed.

units.name: Long vs short 3'UTR isoform overlay
units.what_it_shows: The Fig 2g comparison for the five genes where isoform-resolved data exists: long-UTR and short-UTR NTScore on a shared axis anchored at the stop codon, with ELAVL1 sites between.
units.encoding: Two stacked score tracks plus a site lane; a scope banner stating this is a fixed case study.
units.data_source: /Users/wangyanz/.../figure2/elavl1_isoform_tracks/data/all_utr3_scores.npz (keys BIRC3-LU/SU, CD44-LU/SU, CD47-LU/SU) + ELAVL1_binding_regions.parquet (1,037 rows: start, stop, score, p-value, q-value, matched_sequence, Gene_name).
units.why_it_earns_its_place: The only isoform-resolved data in the project and the basis of a manuscript figure; shipping it as a bounded case study is honest, whereas a generic isoform selector would be empty for 18,088 of 18,093 genes.

units.name: Two-transcript comparison mode
units.what_it_shows: Two transcripts of the same gene stacked on aligned axes, with shared and unique clusters marked.

layout_options.name: A — Unified mRNA browser stack (one continuous axis, overview + detail)
layout_options.pros: The only layout that makes the paper's bilingual claim visible in one glance: protein and UTR motifs share one axis, so coupling arcs are spatially truthful rather than symbolic. Region widths are proportional, so the reader sees that the 3'UTR dominates. The 'no CDS score' hatch turns a data gap into an honest mark instead of a misleading flat line. Overview+detail with one shared viewport is the pattern every genome browser reader already knows (IGV, UCSC, JBrowse), so there is nothing to learn.
layout_options.cons: Requires the projection arithmetic, so a bug there mislocates every protein motif by a factor of three. Mixes a 1-nt and a 3-nt quantum on one axis, which needs the frame ruler to stay honest. The CDS occupies ~62% of the axis for a median transcript while carrying no score and no directly-called nucleotide motifs, so a lot of horizontal space is spent on a region that is mostly a bridge. Dense 3'UTRs (up to 182 motifs) still compress to an unreadable comb at overview zoom.
layout_options.best_for: The paper's reviewers and the computational reader — anyone whose question is 'does the protein↔UTR coupling actually show up in a real transcript?'. Also the best default landing layout, because ACTB demonstrates the top-scoring pair in the whole analysis in a single screen.

layout_options.name: B — Mirrored bilingual (RNA left, protein right, coupling gutter between)
layout_options.pros: Puts the paper's thesis at the centre of the screen literally — the gutter is the finding. Gives each language its own vertical space and its own idiom, so the RNA side can carry CLIP/miRNA lanes and the protein side domains/disorder without competing for width. The gate values sit directly under the arcs, which is where over-reading happens. Scales well when a transcript has many motifs on one side only. Reads well on a laptop because neither column needs the full 1,812-nt axis.
layout_options.cons: Sacrifices true positional comparability: the two sides have different coordinate systems and different lengths, so an arc's endpoints are symbolic, not metric. A reader cannot tell from this layout whether a coupled UTR motif is near the cap or the poly(A) tail relative to the protein motif. The sequence text is demoted below the fold, which conflicts with the literal wording of R1. Degenerates for the 34.8% of transcripts with zero gated pairs — the centre column, the whole point of the layout, is empty.
layout_options.best_for: The reader who arrived from the network view or the abstract and whose question is specifically 'which protein motif goes with which UTR motif in this gene?'. Also the best layout for a talk slide or a figure export.

layout_options.name: C — Reading-first document view (sequence is the primary object)
layout_options.pros: Honours the literal requirement most directly — the sequence IS the page, selectable, copyable, findable with ctrl-F, and printable. The per-line score sparkline keeps the model's evidence adjacent to the residues without a separate scrolling track. Scales gracefully to any length because it is just a document. The codon row makes the protein↔nucleotide correspondence physical at reading scale. Best possible fit for the wet-lab workflow: read, select, copy, order a primer.
layout_options.cons: No transcript-scale gestalt at all — a reader cannot see where they are in a 7,601-nt 3'UTR without scrolling, and the coupling story is nearly invisible because coupled motifs are usually hundreds of lines apart. Annotation lanes have nowhere to live except the right gutter, which caps them at a few chips. Long regions become very long documents (a 7,601-nt 3'UTR is 127 lines). Needs lazy line mounting to stay responsive.
layout_options.best_for: The bench scientist who came to answer 'does my gene have anything, and what is the actual sequence?' — the largest audience by headcount, and the one the other layouts serve worst.

layout_options.name: D — Region-tabbed with sticky inspector (conventional, lowest risk)
layout_options.pros: Lowest implementation risk and the least new vocabulary for a reader — three regions, three tabs, one inspector. Each region gets full width, so a dense 3'UTR is as legible as it can be. The inspector never moves, so clicking a motif does not shift the sequence. Region-specific tracks appear only where they apply (no pLDDT lane on UTR tabs, no CLIP lane on the protein tab), so there are no permanently empty panels. Degrades to a single column on a narrow laptop cleanly.
layout_options.cons: Tabs actively hide the coupling: a protein motif and its paired UTR motif are never on screen together, so the paper's central finding is reduced to a text summary and a link. Loses the transcript-scale gestalt — no sense of proportion between an 84-nt 5'UTR and a 600-nt 3'UTR. Encourages the reader to treat the three regions as three separate datasets, which is precisely the framing the manuscript argues against.
layout_options.best_for: The reader who arrived with a specific motif or a specific region in mind — 'show me the 3'UTR of my gene' — and the safest fallback if the projection arithmetic or the arc layer has to be cut from v1.

layout_options.name: E — Compact progressive single column (laptop and small-screen default)
layout_options.pros: Works at 1280px and below without horizontal scrolling, which matters because the stated reader is a scientist on a laptop. Progressive disclosure means the median transcript (43 motifs) is never dumped on screen at once. The proportional schematic stays pinned at the top so orientation survives collapsing. Bottom-sheet detail avoids the width tax of a sticky rail. Naturally becomes the responsive fallback for every other layout, so it is not wasted work.
layout_options.cons: Collapsed sections hide the comparison the paper is about — coupling becomes a section you open rather than a thing you see. Vertical scrolling replaces spatial reasoning, so cross-region questions require memory. Track stacks are squeezed, so the score track loses vertical resolution and subtle NTScore structure is lost. The annotation lanes have to be demoted to chips.
layout_options.best_for: The default on any screen under ~1400px, and for readers following a link from a phone or a talk. Should be built as the responsive form of A rather than as a separate design.

open_questions: BLOCKING, needs the author: the manuscript says 'MLXIPL ... contains the M2 utr3_0027 motifs (Fig. 4a)', but modules.json assigns utr3_0027 to M1 while the code that produced Fig 4a (build_mlxipl_signatures.py, MLXIPL_M2_signatures.csv) uses utr3_0227, which is M2. MLXIPL is a featured example gene, so its R1 page will contradict either the paper or the data. All evidence points to a one-character typo; confirm before building the M2 example.

Should the unified mRNA axis with projected protein motifs be the default view, or an opt-in mode? I verified the projection is exact (cds == 3*protein+3 in 19,210/19,210; ACTB codons check out), but projecting an amino-acid motif onto nucleotide coordinates is an interpretive act — it asserts that the protein motif 'is' a stretch of mRNA. The paper's framing supports it; the author should confirm the framing is welcome rather than surprising.

How many coupling arcs should be drawn by default? I measured mean 8.04 co-present gated cluster pairs per transcript, median 2, p90 23, max 203 (MRTFB, NCOA1). Top-8 by phylo_corrected_score is my proposal, but the cutoff is an editorial judgement about how much of the transcript's coupling to assert on first paint.

Arcs at cluster level or instance level? I counted cluster pairs. Since a cluster can have several instances on one transcript (ACTB has 4 prot_0040 and 3 utr5_0004 instances), instance-level arcs would multiply. Anchoring one arc per cluster pair at the best-scoring instance is my recommendation, but it under-draws the real co-occurrence and should be labelled as a summary.

The 'no motifs' empty state needs a correct sentence. The surveys' '7,784 nt model context cap' derives from the transcript_length column, which I verified is NOT the mRNA length (ACTB 1,059 vs true 1,812; shorter than utr5+cds+utr3 in all 19,210 rows). What IS transcript_length? Until that is known, the empty state should say 'no motifs were called for this transcript' plus the length comparison (motif-bearing max 11,426 nt vs TTN 109,224 nt) and not assert a hard cap.

Is there a newer or canonical location for the 5'UTR NTScore file? It currently sits at explore_biology/01.protein_localization/analysis/data/h5cache/outputs_utr5_score_0326.h5 — inside an unrelated analysis folder, referenced by no documented pipeline. It has exactly 18,093 keys (a perfect 1:1 with the motif universe), so it is clearly the right file, but its location makes it fragile. The 3'UTR file has 492 extra keys, some length-mismatched, which the build must exclude.

Should the CDS carry any quantitative track at all? There is no per-nucleotide score for CDS or protein anywhere. I propose an explicit hatched 'no score computed' band. If a CDS-level score exists elsewhere or could be generated, it would remove the most visible asymmetry in the view.

Can delta-attention be recomputed for a small set of featured transcripts? Nothing is stored (PANELS.md says Fig 3a is drawn from synthetic data). For the reviewer audience, showing the actual attribution behind a highlight in even 10-20 transcripts would be the highest-value addition to R1 — but it needs GPU inference from the MIRTO checkpoint, not file reads.

Should R1 include a UniProt feature track and a per-residue MobiDB disorder track? Both need new precompute (a corrected UniProt overlap join, ~756k hits, ~2 min; and parsing MobiDB's comma-joined 'start..end' range strings, which I verified are present in the raw TSV). They materially improve the protein half but neither exists today in usable form.

Who curates the ~15-row RBP alias map (U2AF65/U2AF2, TDP43/TARDBP, UNR/CSDE1, IMP3/IGF2BP3, HNRNPH/HNRNPH1, plus opaque 'ACI' and 'SDOS')? Without it every RBP chip and filter in R1 double-counts. It is an afternoon of work but requires someone who knows the nomenclature to sign off.

Is a per-nucleotide score export acceptable to release? The h5 files total 288 MB and represent the model's raw output. Exporting arrays per transcript is trivially easy and scientifically valuable, but it is effectively publishing the model's predictions in bulk — a scope decision, not a technical one.

Should the isoform case study (CD47/CD44/BIRC3 long vs short 3'UTR) be reachable from those genes' R1 pages? The data exists and is isoform-resolved, but the main corpus is one transcript per gene, so a contextual banner on exactly three gene pages is slightly inconsistent. Consistent scoping versus surfacing real data the reader would want.

Confirm the module colour mapping. Three conflicting mappings exist in the tree; I recommend the MCOL used by four published figure scripts (M1 #0072B2, M2 #CC79A7, M3 #E69F00, M4 #D55E00, M5 #4D4D4D, M6 #009E73). If any published figure image is embedded alongside the live view, one of them will need recolouring.
